text: Fill in the blanks to complete the meaning of each hepatitis B serological marker.
questions: HBsAg positivity in serum indicates *active infection:This surface antigen is present whenever the virus is circulating in blood.* with hepatitis B, either acute or chronic.
The presence of anti-HBs antibody signifies *immunity:This neutralising antibody is the goal of vaccination.* to hepatitis B.
HBeAg is a secreted marker of *active viral replication/active replication/viral replication:The 'e' antigen correlates with high viral load and transmission risk.* and high infectivity.
During the window period of acute HBV, the only detectable serological marker is *anti-HBc IgM/Anti-HBc IgM/IgM anti-HBc:HBsAg has cleared but anti-HBs has not yet appeared.*.
Vaccination with recombinant HBsAg generates only *anti-HBs/Anti-HBs:The vaccine contains surface antigen only — no core antigen is encountered.* and never produces anti-HBc.
